findings.title: 3 plaintext credential submission(s) recovered
findings.detail: Form credentials were transmitted unencrypted and are readable from the capture (OWASP A02).

findings.title: All application traffic is cleartext (no TLS)
findings.detail: No HTTPS/TLS traffic was observed; every request, response, and header is exposed.

findings.title: Session cookie 'PHPSESSID' is exposed/replayable
findings.detail: Missing 'Secure' flag — cookie can be sent over plaintext HTTP; Missing 'HttpOnly' flag — cookie readable by JavaScript; No 'SameSite' attribute — cross-site request exposure; Session token replayed in cleartext across 28 requests (replayable/hijackable)

findings.title: Session ID is not regenerated at login (session fixation)
findings.detail: The same session ID was kept across every login; 1 distinct session ID(s) seen in the whole capture (OWASP A07, CWE-384).

findings.title: Session ID survives logout
findings.detail: After /logout the client kept presenting the pre-logout session ID; the token was not rotated or invalidated (CWE-613).

Missing 'HttpOnly' flag — cookie readable by JavaScript
Session token replayed in cleartext across 28 requests (replayable/hijackable)

insights: 22/22 TCP flows last ~5.0s from SYN to FIN regardless of how much data they carry: connection lifetime is set by the HTTP keep-alive idle timeout (about 5s), not by user activity. Every connection is closed 5.00–5.02s after its last data packet; in 6 flows both FINs cross on the wire (simultaneous close), so client and server time out together.
Traffic is strongly asymmetric: 93.1% of bytes flow server-to-client (page and image downloads), 6.9% client-to-server.
The two largest flows (#7, #6) carry 73.3% of all TCP bytes: GET /docs/graphics/docker/detail.png; GET /instructions.php, GET /docs/graphics/docker/overview.png.
The browser opened up to 2 parallel TCP connections (peak at ~48s) to fetch embedded resources concurrently.
Connections are reused for up to 2 requests (HTTP/1.1 persistent connections).
Every TCP flow has a complete three-way handshake and an orderly FIN teardown; no resets, scans or half-open connections were observed.
100% of TCP flows are cleartext HTTP on port 80; no flow is encrypted.

The server's packets arrive with TTL 63 while the client's leave with 64: both look like Linux (initial TTL 64), but the server sits 1 routed hop away despite sharing the subnet, consistent with DVWA running in a container behind the VM's bridge.
Every MAC address is locally administered (randomised/virtual), as expected for VM network adapters; no vendor OUI is present.
A third device (3e:06:30:63:f6:65) only sends IPv6 router advertisements to ff02::1: the hypervisor's virtual-network gateway, not a participant in the session.

39 frames are larger than the 1,514-byte Ethernet MTU (up to 33,090 B): an artefact of segmentation offload (GRO/LRO) on the capturing NIC, not jumbo frames on the wire. Byte counts are right; per-frame counts are understated.
TCP health is clean: handshake RTT 0.693–4.158 ms (median 1.777 ms), 0 retransmissions, 0 zero-window events. The slowest server response is POST /login.php at 71.913 ms.
Separated by idle gaps of ≥10s, the session forms 7 activity bursts; the median time between new connections is 11.224s, a human browsing pace rather than automated traffic.
Only 2 IPv4 hosts exchange application traffic; the remaining frames are link-local ARP / IPv6 neighbour-discovery noise.
